blocks.md: This lesson follows **Fallacies and Pitfalls** in *Agent Economics* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Economics, § Fallacies and Pitfalls
blocks.md: An economic evaluation can be mathematically precise yet misleading if it tracks the wrong unit of work or quietly shifts the standard of acceptance. In agent systems, these errors typically occur when localized metrics, such as a model's raw token tariff, an isolated inference speedup, or a child agent's premature stopping condition, substitute for the end-to-end cost of completed, accepted tasks.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.
A one-time adaptation investment recovers its cost after N* = C_adapt / (C_base - C_adapted) tasks, never if the per-task saving is nonpositive, and only while acceptance stays equal.
Speculative decoding pays only when the accepted-draft rate shortens the output-bound critical path by more than draft and verification work add to the bill.
Owning capacity beats an API at a delivered utilization u* = F / (3600 R (P_eff - v)), not at a token price.
